findings.issue: SetupPackage.ExtractTo now deletes the file of the entry that failed its size/hash check, but every entry written before it is left on disk — and setup.json is the first entry in the manifest, so a container refused on its second or later entry leaves the cleartext deviceSeed and officeKey behind in the target folder while the caller sees only an exception. The new test A_tampered_entry_leaves_no_partial_file_at_the_extraction_target asserts only that logo.png is gone; setup.json is still there. The XML doc states the residue as intended behaviour, so B1 can only get this right if it is told.
findings.fix: In the ExtractTo XML doc on SetupPackage (and on ContainerReader.ExtractTo), state explicitly that on a CryptoException the caller must delete the whole target directory, because entries already written include setup.json with the device seed and office key in the clear; or, better, have SetupPackage.ExtractTo extract into a freshly created subdirectory and, on failure, delete that directory before rethrowing (Directory.Delete(dir, recursive: true) inside the same best-effort TryDelete pattern). Add a test asserting that setup.json is absent after a refused extraction.

findings.issue: In Inspect(Stream, ..., ownsStream) the new Validate(expectations) throw (missing StagingDirectory, and the pre-existing pinned-key-length and skew throws) happens before the container is opened and outside any try/catch, so a caller that passed ownsStream: true has already handed over the stream but gets it back open and leaked. The path form is safe (it disposes its own FileStream), and the new test only exercises the path form, so this is unpinned.
findings.fix: Wrap Validate(expectations) in try { Validate(expectations); } catch { if (ownsStream) { stream.Dispose(); } throw; } in Inspect(Stream, ...), matching the disposal contract the rest of the method already honours, and extend The_setup_reader_refuses_to_run_without_its_own_staging_folder with a stream case asserting the stream is closed after the throw.

missing_spec_items: None of the nine items of this package's specification is missing: (1) gating, (2) required staging, (5) Argon2 floor, (6) ReadTo + documented cache threshold, (7) Expired -> Package/FutureDate with Signature Ok, (8) 1 MB manifest/signature bound, (9) letterTemplate + letter-template.docx round trip with and without — all implemented and each pinned by a test.

notes:
COMMANDS. Ran exactly `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Crypto` then `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests` from D:\AI\Administration2. Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) under TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. Tests: Failed 0, Passed 230, Skipped 0, Total 230 — the prior round's 224 baseline plus 6 new facts; the earlier 212-test baseline is fully contained and nothing regressed. I modified no file and ran no git command beyond read-only status/diff. No WPF host or Blazor page in this package, so the host-launch rule does not apply; I viewed W03 light and dark anyway, which is what produced the two carry-over items above.

SPEC ITEM BY ITEM, all verified against the code and against the review file the spec cites.
(1) Read, ReadTo, ExtractTo and the Content property all call Checks.EnsureAcceptable() first; ReadLogo/ReadGuide/ReadReportTemplate/ReadLetterTemplate go through TryRead -> Read, so they are gated too. The single exception is explicitly named ReadLogoPreviewFromRejectedFile, and its XML doc justifies it properly: a SetupPackage only exists after the container signature, the certificate chain and the package password have all held, and the logo is the one entry of the format that carries no secret. The new Description property is the right answer to the same problem for text — it is built in the constructor from the parsed content and deliberately omits DeviceSeed, OfficeKey and Revocation, so a refusal screen can name the organisation, office, device and employee without the secrets ever becoming reachable. Pinned by No_entry_may_be_read_out_of_a_file_whose_checks_did_not_all_pass and The_device_seed_and_office_key_stay_out_of_reach_of_a_refused_file_while_its_description_does_not.
(2) SetupPackageReader.Validate and SetupPackageWriter.Prepare both throw CryptoException(Corrupt) on a null or empty StagingDirectory, before anything is opened or staged, and both XML docs say why (setup.json is staged in the clear and carries the device seed and the office key). ContainerWriter.CreateStagingFile is the only %TEMP% fallback and is now unreachable from either setup path. Both refusals are tested, and the writer's internal self-check no longer smuggles a null through — the removal of the parameterless SetupExpectations.FirstRun property in favour of FirstRun(stagingDirectory) closes the landmine the previous round left for B1.
(3) Argon2: SetupWriteRequest.Kdf is now internal and BuildRequest substitutes Argon2Params.CreateDefault() when it is absent, so no assembly outside Wakeel.Crypto (and the test assembly that shares InternalsVisibleTo) can ship a production setup file at a weakened cost. The_writer_uses_the_products_full_argon2_cost_when_no_internal_test_hook_is_supplied reads the cost back out of the written manifest and asserts DefaultMemoryKb/Iterations/Parallelism, which is a real assertion, not a tautology. I grepped for Kdf across src/ and tests/: nothing outside Wakeel.Crypto and its own test project sets it, so making it internal breaks no existing caller. The read side is unaffected — the ceiling in Argon2Params.Validate (with its own test, A_file_that_demands_an_absurd_amount_of_work_to_open_is_refused) still bounds what a hostile file may demand.
(4) Streaming and cache: ContainerReader.ReadEntryTo copies through HashingStream with CopyWithLimit(expected.Size) and checks size and hash after the copy; SetupPackage.ReadTo forwards to it, gated, and never touches the cache. HashingStream's leaveOpen defaults to true, so a caller's destination stream is not closed behind its back — I checked, because that would have been a silent trap. MaxCachedEntrySize is documented and the comparison is now >= , matching both the doc ("At or above it") and the test name; the test covers all three sides of the boundary (below: Assert.Same; exactly at: Assert.NotSame; above: Assert.NotSame) with Assert.Equal on the bytes so it cannot pass by returning garbage.
(5) Expired -> FutureDate: correct, and I checked the premise rather than the comment. CertificateChain raises ErrorCode.Expired for three reasons — certificate dated in the future, certificate older than maxAge, revocation list dated outside its window — and in the setup path maxAge and maxRevocationListAge are both null (the 4-argument TryVerify overload defaults them), while a badly dated revocation list is caught by CheckRevocation first and never reaches CheckDevice. So in this path Expired can only mean "dated ahead of this clock", and translating it to FutureDate on Package (root) and on Device (device certificate) is sound rather than a mislabel. Both translations have their own test that isolates the date: WriteWithRootIssuedAt dates only the root, and the device test re-issues only the device certificate three days ahead with everything else at Now.
(6) Manifest bound: ReadAll(entry, 1 MB) enforces the limit while the bytes are still being inflated, not against the declared size, so a deflate bomb is refused after ~1 MB + one 80 KB chunk. The test pads a field the schema ignores to 2 MB and re-zips, which compresses to almost nothing — exactly the shape the bound exists for — and the signature test is the sibling case. Both assert ErrorCode.Corrupt.
(7) Letter template: SetupEntryNames.LetterTemplate, SetupIncludes.LetterTemplate, SetupCheckItem.LetterTemplate (placed after ReportTemplate, so the enum's display order is still the screen's), the writer's Add, the checker's Optional and the allow-list of permitted entry names are all updated coherently; an undeclared letter-template.docx is refused as Tampered, exactly like the other three. Round trips exist both with it (all four optional entries, all check items Ok, Enum.GetValues length asserted against the list count) and without it (Absent). ARCHITECTURE §4 already names includes.letterTemplate and letter-template.docx, so the docs needed no change and none was made.

SECURITY, what I checked rather than took on trust. Verify before decrypt still holds: ContainerReader.Open parses and shape-checks the manifest, hashes the payload and verifies the Ed25519 signature before returning; Examine then requires DeviceKind.Org, runs the chain against the pinned key where there is one, and only then derives the content key and decrypts setup.json. No new call site decrypts earlier than that, the logo preview included. Cleartext staging cannot reach %TEMP% from either setup entry point any more. Manifest reads are bounded. The KDF floor cannot be weakened from outside the assembly. The two secrets are unreachable from a refused file through every public surface I could find: Content, Read, TryRead, the four named readers, ReadTo and ExtractTo are all gated, and Description carries neither. The logo preview is bounded twice — by the manifest-declared size against MaxLogoSize before any decryption, and by CopyWithLimit(expected.Size) during it — and refuses an entry the description never declared, so it cannot be used as a read primitive for an entry the check list already called Tampered.

TEST QUALITY. The six new tests all assert behaviour that would change if the code were reverted. Two of them do manifest surgery and re-sign with the organisation key so that the container still opens and only the rule under test fires, which is the right way to isolate a post-signature rule. FirstRun_builds_expectations_that_carry_only_the_staging_folder is the weakest of the six (it pins a factory's shape), but it is cheap and it does prevent the removed property from quietly coming back. No test asserts something it just computed.

FOR THE B1 ADMIN / FIRST-RUN BUILDERS — the public API deltas that matter to you. (a) SetupExpectations.FirstRun is now a method taking the staging folder, not a property; StagingDirectory is mandatory for both SetupPackageReader.Inspect/Open and SetupPackageWriter.Write and must be the product's own protected folder, never a temporary one. (b) SetupWriteRequest.Kdf is internal: A08 gets the product's real Argon2 cost, so the export step takes a visible fraction of a second — show the wait. (c) SetupPackage.Content now throws when the checks did not all pass; use the new SetupPackage.Description for everything W03 renders next to the refusal, and ReadLogoPreviewFromRejectedFile for the logo on that screen. (d) SetupPackage.ReadTo(entryName, Stream) is the way to take the guide and the two templates out without buffering them; on an exception, discard what was written. (e) SetupCheckItem gained LetterTemplate, so the enum's length changed — do not hard-code the number of rows. (f) On a failed ExtractTo, delete the target folder yourself (finding 1).
